This report is based on a visual review of the building at 1450 W 64th St in Vancouver, BC, known as Joy Kogawa House. The building is a 2 storey wood structure residential style house originally built in 1906. The site also includes a detached wood framed garage. 

Overall the building is in good condition with a Facility Condition Index (FCI) score of 4.9% and no significant deficiencies noted. However, if the recommended replacements and repairs are not carried out within the next year, we expect that the building will reach fair condition with an FCI of 7.4% in 2015. The exterior walls are currently in fair condition with decayed wood trim and cracks noted in the stucco finish. The roof is reported in good condition however the flashing around the chimney needs to be replaced. Overall the architectural components are reported in good to fair condition. The mechanical equipment in the building is all reported in good condition. The electrical equipment in the building is all reported in good to fair condition.

Below is a summary of major actions we recommend within the next 5 years, based on our visual inspection on May 6, 2014. The total estimated cost all of these actions is $22,000.

Action Urgency: Immediately
B2010 - Exterior Walls - Repair the wood trim - $1,000
B30 - Roofing - Repair flashing around the chimney - $1,000
G2040 - Site Development - Repair wood deck and staircase - $1,500

TOTAL = $7,000

There was some cracking noted in the stucco exterior wall finish. There was some decay noted in the exterior wood trim. We recommend repairing these items pending the results of a Building Envelope Condition Assessment (BECA). The vinyl siding on the building is in good condition. The building has 6 single plane windows and 13 insulated glass windows. The single plane windows have attained their designed service life and remain functional but consideration should be taken to replace them with a more thermally efficient style. The roof was replaced in 2012 and is in excellent condition, however there are reportedly leaks around the chimney. We recommend repairing the flashing around the chimney as soon as possible.

All of the interior finishes and fittings are reported in good condition. Many finishes were upgraded in 2004 during a major renovation.

The building site includes a detached wood framed garage. The exterior walls of the garage are reported in poor condition, and the roof is reported in fair condition. We recommend upgrading these items in the near future to avoid further deterioration. The site also contains a concrete walkways which is reported in fair condition. There is a concrete retaining wall on site which is experiencing localized cracking and reported in fair condition. We recommend repairs to this retaining wall. The site has a small wood framed fence which is reported in poor condition with decay observed. There is a wood deck and staircase at the rear of the building reported in fair condition and requiring some repairs.

No significant deficiencies were observed to suggest differential settlement of the building foundations or movement of the building structure. 

The building exterior walls are generally comprised of stone veneer panels and window walls on the building elevations. The exterior entrance doors are folding glass doors set in aluminum frames. The service doors are hollow metal doors in metal frames. The roof cover includes green roof assemblies. Overall, the building envelope components appear to be in good condition. 

The interior finishes in the building include ceramic floor tiles, sealed concrete floor finish, painted wall finish,  exposed concrete ceiling. The interior finishes appear to be in good condition overall.

The two-storey building appears to be constructed on spread concrete footings with a slab on grade. The superstructure seems to be of wood walls, wood beams and wood joists supporting a wood deck floor.  No significant deficiencies were observed to suggest differential settlement of the building foundations or movement of the building structure.
 
The building's exterior walls generally comprise of wood and vinyl siding, veneer stone and painted wall finishes on the building elevations. The windows are vinyl double-paned glass units and single-paned glass set in painted wood frames. The commercial units have a glass doors set in aluminum frame and residential and commercial have wood doors in wood frames. The roof covers include 2-ply modified bituminous at the flat roof assembly. Overall, the building envelope components appear to be in good condition except the exterior painted walls and exterior wood doors are in fair condition. 

The interior finishes in the building include ceramic floor tiles, laminate wood flooring, painted wall assemblies, and painted ceiling assemblies. Overall, the interior finishes appear to be in fair condition.

The superstructure seems to be of concrete masonry walls and metal beams supporting a suspended wood floor and wood roof deck.  No significant deficiencies were observed to suggest differential settlement of the building foundations or movement of the building structure.
 
The building's exterior walls generally comprise of painted masonry walls on the building elevations. The windows are single-paned glass set in painted wood and metal frames. At the main entrances glass doors are set in aluminum and wood frames, and the service doors are metal doors in painted metal frames. The roof includes a modified bituminous at the flat roof assembly. Overall, the building envelope components appear to be in good condition except the exterior painted walls and the exterior doors which are in fair condition.

The interior finishes in the building include ceramic floor tiles, wood flooring, painted wall assemblies, painted ceiling assemblies. Overall, the interior finishes appear to be in fair condition.
